clips.send: Bladder. Stores urine. A stretchy muscular bag. It can hold about 400–600 mL.
clips.text: Bladder. Stores urine. A stretchy muscular bag.. It can hold about 400–600 mL.

clips.send: Diaphragm. The breathing muscle. A dome-shaped muscle under the lungs. When it contracts it flattens, the chest gets bigger and air rushes in. Hiccups are diaphragm spasms!
clips.text: Diaphragm. The breathing muscle. A dome-shaped muscle under the lungs.. When it contracts it flattens, the chest gets bigger and air rushes in. Hiccups are diaphragm spasms!

clips.send: Nervous system. Senses, controls and coordinates the body. The brain, spinal cord and nerves carry electrical signals. Signals can travel about 120 m/s, faster than a race car. Reflexes (like pulling your hand off a hot pan) go through the spinal cord before the brain even knows.
clips.text: Nervous system. Senses, controls and coordinates the body. The brain, spinal cord and nerves carry electrical signals.. Signals can travel about 120 m/s, faster than a race car.. Reflexes (like pulling your hand off a hot pan) go through the spinal cord before the brain even knows.

clips.send: Large intestine. Absorbs water and forms feces. About 1.5 m long but wider than the small intestine. Helpful bacteria here make some vitamins.
clips.text: Large intestine. Absorbs water and forms feces. About 1.5 m long but wider than the small intestine.. Helpful bacteria here make some vitamins.

clips.send: Esophagus. Food tube to the stomach. About 25 cm long. Waves of muscle (peristalsis) push food down, even if you are upside down!
clips.text: Esophagus. Food tube to the stomach. About 25 cm long.. Waves of muscle (peristalsis) push food down, even if you are upside down!

clips.send: Bones. Skull, spine, ribs and limb bones. The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone. The spine is made of 33 vertebrae.
clips.text: Bones. Skull, spine, ribs and limb bones. The femur (thigh bone) is the longest and strongest bone.. The spine is made of 33 vertebrae.

clips.send: Lungs. Where gas exchange happens. Hundreds of millions of alveoli give a surface area of about half a tennis court. The left lung is a bit smaller to make room for the heart.
clips.text: Lungs. Where gas exchange happens. Hundreds of millions of alveoli give a surface area of about half a tennis court.. The left lung is a bit smaller to make room for the heart.

clips.send: Brain. The control center. About 86 billion neurons. Uses about 20 percent of the body’s energy. Cerebrum: thinking, cerebellum: balance, brainstem: heartbeat and breathing.
clips.text: Brain. The control center. About 86 billion neurons.. Uses about 20% of the body’s energy.. Cerebrum: thinking · cerebellum: balance · brainstem: heartbeat and breathing.

clips.send: Blood vessels. Arteries, veins and capillaries. Lined up end to end, your blood vessels would wrap around Earth more than twice. In the model, red equals oxygen-rich blood, blue equals oxygen-poor blood.
clips.text: Blood vessels. Arteries, veins and capillaries. Lined up end to end, your blood vessels would wrap around Earth more than twice.. In the model, red = oxygen-rich blood, blue = oxygen-poor blood.

clips.send: Liver. Makes bile and cleans the blood. The largest internal organ. Bile helps break fats into tiny droplets. Stores nutrients and removes toxins from the blood.
clips.text: Liver. Makes bile and cleans the blood. The largest internal organ.. Bile helps break fats into tiny droplets.. Stores nutrients and removes toxins from the blood.

clips.send: Trachea (windpipe). Air tube to the lungs. C-shaped rings of cartilage keep it open. It splits into two bronchi, one for each lung.
clips.text: Trachea (windpipe). Air tube to the lungs. C-shaped rings of cartilage keep it open.. It splits into two bronchi, one for each lung.

clips.send: Respiratory system. Takes in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide. Air path: nose/mouth, trachea, bronchi, millions of tiny air sacs (alveoli). In the alveoli, O2 moves into the blood and CO2 moves out. Breathing is driven by the diaphragm muscle.
clips.text: Respiratory system. Takes in oxygen and removes carbon dioxide. Air path: nose/mouth → trachea → bronchi → millions of tiny air sacs (alveoli).. In the alveoli, O₂ moves into the blood and CO₂ moves out.. Breathing is driven by the diaphragm muscle.

clips.send: Digestive system. Breaks food into nutrients and absorbs them. Mechanical digestion (chewing, churning) and chemical digestion (enzymes, acid) work together. The small intestine is about 6 m long; its villi absorb nutrients into the blood. The large intestine absorbs water from what is left.
clips.text: Digestive system. Breaks food into nutrients and absorbs them. Mechanical digestion (chewing, churning) and chemical digestion (enzymes, acid) work together.. The small intestine is about 6 m long; its villi absorb nutrients into the blood.. The large intestine absorbs water from what is left.

clips.send: Stomach. Churns food with acid and enzymes. Strong acid kills most germs in food. After 2–4 hours food becomes a soupy mix called chyme. A layer of mucus stops the stomach from digesting itself.
clips.text: Stomach. Churns food with acid and enzymes. Strong acid kills most germs in food.. After 2–4 hours food becomes a soupy mix called chyme.. A layer of mucus stops the stomach from digesting itself.

clips.send: Small intestine. Finishes digestion and absorbs nutrients. About 6 m long, folded up in your belly. Millions of finger-like villi pass nutrients into the blood.
clips.text: Small intestine. Finishes digestion and absorbs nutrients. About 6 m long, folded up in your belly.. Millions of finger-like villi pass nutrients into the blood.

clips.send: Circulatory system. Transports oxygen, nutrients and wastes. The heart beats about 100,000 times a day. Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back. Tiny capillaries are where oxygen and nutrients pass into cells.
clips.text: Circulatory system. Transports oxygen, nutrients and wastes. The heart beats about 100,000 times a day.. Arteries carry blood away from the heart; veins carry it back.. Tiny capillaries are where oxygen and nutrients pass into cells.

clips.send: Lymph nodes and vessels. Filter fluid and trap germs. Hundreds of bean-sized nodes, packed with white blood cells. They often swell when you are fighting an infection.
clips.text: Lymph nodes & vessels. Filter fluid and trap germs. Hundreds of bean-sized nodes, packed with white blood cells.. They often swell when you are fighting an infection.

clips.send: Heart. A muscular pump with 4 chambers. 2 atria receive blood; 2 ventricles pump it out. The right side pumps blood to the lungs; the left side pumps it to the whole body. About the size of your fist; the left ventricle has the thickest wall.
clips.text: Heart. A muscular pump with 4 chambers. 2 atria receive blood; 2 ventricles pump it out.. The right side pumps blood to the lungs; the left side pumps it to the whole body.. About the size of your fist; the left ventricle has the thickest wall.

clips.send: 神经。在全身各处传递信号。感觉神经把感官获得的信息传进来。运动神经把指令传给肌肉。
clips.text: 神经. 在全身各处传递信号. 感觉神经把感官获得的信息传进来。. 运动神经把指令传给肌肉。

clips.send: 肾脏。过滤血液，形成尿液。两个豆子形状的器官，靠近后背，每个约拳头大小。每个肾脏里大约有一百万个微小的过滤单位（肾单位）。
clips.text: 肾脏. 过滤血液，形成尿液. 两个豆子形状的器官，靠近后背，每个约拳头大小。. 每个肾脏里大约有一百万个微小的过滤单位（肾单位）。

clips.send: 胃。用胃酸和消化酶搅拌食物。强酸能杀死食物中的大部分病菌。2 到 4 小时后，食物变成粥状的食糜。一层黏液保护胃壁，防止胃把自己消化掉。
clips.text: 胃. 用胃酸和消化酶搅拌食物. 强酸能杀死食物中的大部分病菌。. 2 到 4 小时后，食物变成粥状的食糜。. 一层黏液保护胃壁，防止胃把自己消化掉。

clips.send: 脑。控制中心。大约有 860 亿个神经元。消耗全身约 百分之20 的能量。大脑负责思考，小脑负责平衡，脑干控制心跳和呼吸。
clips.text: 脑. 控制中心. 大约有 860 亿个神经元。. 消耗全身约 20% 的能量。. 大脑负责思考，小脑负责平衡，脑干控制心跳和呼吸。

clips.send: 食管。把食物送到胃的管道。长约 25 厘米。肌肉一波一波地收缩（蠕动），把食物向下推，即使你倒立也可以！
clips.text: 食管. 把食物送到胃的管道. 长约 25 厘米。. 肌肉一波一波地收缩（蠕动），把食物向下推，即使你倒立也可以！

clips.send: 小肠。完成消化并吸收营养物质。长约 6 米，盘曲在腹腔中。数百万个手指状的小肠绒毛把营养物质送入血液。
clips.text: 小肠. 完成消化并吸收营养物质. 长约 6 米，盘曲在腹腔中。. 数百万个手指状的小肠绒毛把营养物质送入血液。

clips.send: 淋巴结与淋巴管。过滤淋巴液，拦截病原体。全身有数百个豆子大小的淋巴结，里面聚集着大量白细胞。身体对抗感染时，淋巴结常常会肿大。
clips.text: 淋巴结与淋巴管. 过滤淋巴液，拦截病原体. 全身有数百个豆子大小的淋巴结，里面聚集着大量白细胞。. 身体对抗感染时，淋巴结常常会肿大。

clips.send: 大肠。吸收水分，形成粪便。长约 1.5 米，但比小肠粗。这里的有益细菌能制造一些维生素。
clips.text: 大肠. 吸收水分，形成粪便. 长约 1.5 米，但比小肠粗。. 这里的有益细菌能制造一些维生素。

clips.send: 呼吸系统。吸入氧气，排出二氧化碳。空气的路线：鼻/口，气管，支气管，数以亿计的微小肺泡。在肺泡中，氧气进入血液，二氧化碳离开血液。呼吸运动主要靠膈肌的收缩和舒张。
clips.text: 呼吸系统. 吸入氧气，排出二氧化碳. 空气的路线：鼻/口 → 气管 → 支气管 → 数以亿计的微小肺泡。. 在肺泡中，氧气进入血液，二氧化碳离开血液。. 呼吸运动主要靠膈肌的收缩和舒张。

clips.send: 神经系统。感受刺激，控制和协调全身。脑、脊髓和神经负责传递电信号。信号的传导速度可达每秒约 120 米，比赛车还快。反射（比如手碰到烫锅立刻缩回）经过脊髓完成，大脑还没“意识到”就已经发生了。
clips.text: 神经系统. 感受刺激，控制和协调全身. 脑、脊髓和神经负责传递电信号。. 信号的传导速度可达每秒约 120 米，比赛车还快。. 反射（比如手碰到烫锅立刻缩回）经过脊髓完成，大脑还没“意识到”就已经发生了。

clips.send: 循环系统。运输氧气、营养物质和废物。心脏每天大约跳动 10 万次。动脉把血液运离心脏，静脉把血液送回心脏。细小的毛细血管是氧气和营养物质进入细胞的地方。
clips.text: 循环系统. 运输氧气、营养物质和废物. 心脏每天大约跳动 10 万次。. 动脉把血液运离心脏，静脉把血液送回心脏。. 细小的毛细血管是氧气和营养物质进入细胞的地方。

clips.send: 血管。动脉、静脉和毛细血管。把全身的血管首尾相连，可以绕地球两圈多。模型中红色表示富含氧的血液，蓝色表示含氧少的血液。
clips.text: 血管. 动脉、静脉和毛细血管. 把全身的血管首尾相连，可以绕地球两圈多。. 模型中红色表示富含氧的血液，蓝色表示含氧少的血液。

clips.send: 膈（膈肌）。负责呼吸的肌肉。位于肺下方的穹顶形肌肉。它收缩时变平，胸腔扩大，空气就被吸进来。打嗝就是膈肌痉挛！
clips.text: 膈（膈肌）. 负责呼吸的肌肉. 位于肺下方的穹顶形肌肉。. 它收缩时变平，胸腔扩大，空气就被吸进来。打嗝就是膈肌痉挛！

clips.send: 肝脏。分泌胆汁，净化血液。人体最大的内脏器官。胆汁帮助把脂肪分散成微小的颗粒。储存营养物质，并清除血液中的有毒物质。
clips.text: 肝脏. 分泌胆汁，净化血液. 人体最大的内脏器官。. 胆汁帮助把脂肪分散成微小的颗粒。. 储存营养物质，并清除血液中的有毒物质。

clips.send: 肺。进行气体交换的场所。数亿个肺泡的总面积约相当于半个网球场。左肺比右肺稍小，为心脏留出空间。
clips.text: 肺. 进行气体交换的场所. 数亿个肺泡的总面积约相当于半个网球场。. 左肺比右肺稍小，为心脏留出空间。

clips.send: 骨。颅骨、脊柱、肋骨和四肢骨。股骨（大腿骨）是最长、最结实的骨。脊柱由 33 块椎骨组成。
clips.text: 骨. 颅骨、脊柱、肋骨和四肢骨. 股骨（大腿骨）是最长、最结实的骨。. 脊柱由 33 块椎骨组成。

clips.send: 气管。通往肺的空气管道。C 形的软骨环使气管保持畅通。它分成两条支气管，分别通向左右两肺。
clips.text: 气管. 通往肺的空气管道. C 形的软骨环使气管保持畅通。. 它分成两条支气管，分别通向左右两肺。

clips.send: 心脏。有四个腔的肌肉泵。两个心房接收血液，两个心室把血液泵出去。右心把血液泵向肺，左心把血液泵向全身。大约和你的拳头一样大；左心室的壁最厚。
clips.text: 心脏. 有四个腔的肌肉泵. 两个心房接收血液，两个心室把血液泵出去。. 右心把血液泵向肺，左心把血液泵向全身。. 大约和你的拳头一样大；左心室的壁最厚。

clips.send: 消化系统。把食物分解成营养物质并吸收。物理性消化（咀嚼、搅拌）和化学性消化（消化酶、胃酸）共同进行。小肠长约 6 米，小肠绒毛把营养物质吸收进血液。大肠从剩下的食物残渣中吸收水分。
clips.text: 消化系统. 把食物分解成营养物质并吸收. 物理性消化（咀嚼、搅拌）和化学性消化（消化酶、胃酸）共同进行。. 小肠长约 6 米，小肠绒毛把营养物质吸收进血液。. 大肠从剩下的食物残渣中吸收水分。

clips.send: 膀胱。储存尿液。一个有弹性的肌肉囊。大约能容纳 400 到 600 毫升尿液。
